verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew safely splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026, at 5:07 p.m. PDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'splashdown off the coast of San Diego, expected around 5 p.m. Pacific time Friday... around 5:07 p.m.'; R4: 'splashdown off the coast of San Diego... at 8:07 p.m. EDT / 5:07 PDT'; R1/R5: safe splashdown in Pacific off San Diego, April 10, 2026.
verifications.reasoning: All details directly match: location, date, time in PDT, and safe splashdown confirmed across sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and timezone directly stated in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft named "Integrity" completed a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Orion capsule, named "Integrity"... 10-day mission'; R1: '10-day journey'; R5/R6: '10-day mission... Integrity'.
verifications.reasoning: Name and mission duration directly confirmed.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft landed roughly 60 miles off the San Diego coast.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4: 'around 50 nautical miles off the coast of San Diego' (50 nautical miles ≈ 57.5 statute miles).
verifications.reasoning: Source specifies ~50 nautical miles (roughly 58 miles), supporting 'roughly 60 miles' but less precise and units differ slightly.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft landed for recovery by the U.S. Navy.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'U.S. Navy recovery vessel'; R2: 'Navy divers... U.S.S. John P. Murtha'; R4/R5: 'U.S. Navy... recover'.
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of U.S. Navy recovery role.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II splashdown occurred in the Pacific Ocean approximately 50-60 nautical miles off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'splashdown around 50 nautical miles off the coast of San Diego'.
verifications.reasoning: 'Around 50 nautical miles' directly supports 'approximately 50-60 nautical miles' as the range encompasses the stated distance.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II splashdown occurred on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8:07 p.m. ET Friday, April 10, 2026'; R4: 'April 10, 2026' (context confirms Friday).

verifications.claim: The U.S. Navy ship USS John P. Murtha was positioned to recover the Artemis II crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'U.S.S. John P. Murtha... for an immediate medical evaluation'; R4: 'USS John P. Murtha... recovery ship'; R5: 'USS John P. Murtha'.
verifications.reasoning: Exact ship and recovery role directly confirmed.

verifications.claim: The capsule performed a "skip entry" technique to manage heat and reduce landing loads.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'dip into the atmosphere, then pop up again — like a stone skipping... to reduce heat stress and G-force... this time the “skip” will be brief'; R2: 'new, more direct reentry technique'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe modified skip entry for heat management, directly supporting the claim.

verifications.claim: After landing, the capsule inflated five orange airbags.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'five orange airbags will inflate around the top'; R5: 'Orion's five airbags have inflated'.
verifications.reasoning: Exact details of five airbags inflating post-landing confirmed.

verifications.claim: The five orange airbags turned the spacecraft into an upright position for astronaut exit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'five orange airbags... flip the capsule into an upright position, making the exit easier'; R5: 'landed in the Pacific Ocean upright'.
verifications.reasoning: Direct description of airbags flipping capsule upright for exit.
